key_insight: Geometry-optimized hyperbolic surface codes can significantly improve fault-tolerance efficiency, doubling code distance and quadrupling efficiency at fixed qubit count and check weight.
engineering_relevance: The work supports modular quantum hardware by pairing high-efficiency error correction with a routing strategy that makes hyperbolic codes more practical for planar, large-scale architectures.
method: Construct finite families of hyperbolic surface codes with optimized periodic identifications.
Design a topology-aware partitioning algorithm to split codes into bounded planar modules.
Evaluate modular vs. monolithic layouts under circuit-level Monte Carlo simulation.
evidence_signal: Circuit-level Monte Carlo results report finite-size threshold estimates for both layouts, and increasing long-range gate error by 3× only mildly lowers the estimated thresholds.
watch_item: The routing and threshold benefits depend on managing long-range communication and hardware error rates, so practical deployment may still be constrained by interconnect fidelity and modular integration complexity.
paper_title: Geometry-optimized hyperbolic codes for modular fault-tolerant quantum architectures
